pages.text:
Livhu is a happy girl who enjoys soaking
up the sun and watching flowers bloom
brightly in her garden.
She also enjoys going outside
in her wheelchair.
pages.change: Livhu is introduced: a happy girl who loves her garden and going out in her wheelchair
pages.question_created: What happens when she goes outside?
pages.page_turn_note: The last line points outside; the next spread takes her there.

notes: Livhu, drawn with a smiling sun for a head, waters purple flowers from a sticker-covered wheelchair
illustration.only_in_image: Livhu, like every person in the book, is drawn with a sky body for a head: hers is a smiling sun; her wheelchair is covered in stickers.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
When she is outside, some people
stare at her.
“Aww!”
they say, feeling sorry for her.
pages.change: Outside, adults stare at her and pity her
pages.question_created: How does Livhu feel about being pitied?
pages.page_turn_note: The text gives only the onlookers' feeling; the turn moves to her own voice.

notes: three grown-ups with grey moon-like heads stare and point from a grassy slope; Livhu looks sad and blushes
illustration.only_in_image: Livhu's own feeling: she looks down, sad and blushing, while one adult points and another covers his mouth; the text tells only what the onlookers feel.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“But I want to stay and
talk to people,”
Livhu says to the cashier who wheels her
to the front of the line in the spaza shop.
pages.action: is wheeled to the front of the queue
pages.change: A cashier pushes her past the queue without asking, and she says she would rather stay and talk
pages.question_created: Will anyone ask her what she wants?
pages.page_turn_note: Her objection ends the spread unanswered.

notes: a smiling cashier pushes Livhu's wheelchair under a SPAZA sign; Livhu frowns, one hand reaching back
illustration.only_in_image: The cashier smiles kindly while pushing, and Livhu frowns with an arm reaching back: well-meant help she did not choose.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“May we push you down
the slope?”
offer some of the kids in the park.
pages.location: top of a slope in the park
pages.change: Children in the park ask her permission before helping
pages.page_turn_note: A question to Livhu ends the spread; the answer comes after the turn as a sound and a ride.

notes: two children with planet heads, one holding flowers, stand behind Livhu at the top of a green slope; she raises both arms
illustration.only_in_image: Livhu answers with both arms raised in a yes; the text never gives her reply.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Swishhhh!”
Livhu feels the fresh air whip across her
face as they go down the hill.
pages.change: Helped the way she agreed to, she flies down the hill
pages.page_turn_note: A full-bleed ride spread; the turn brings a reflective statement.

notes: seen from above, Livhu rolls through flowers and stones with arms spread wide, beaming
illustration.only_in_image: Seen from directly above, she spreads both arms wide among flowers and stones: the speed and joy are in the pose and point of view.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Livhu knows people want to help,
BUT…
pages.change: The narrator states that she knows people want to help, and stops on a BUT
pages.page_turn_note: The sentence breaks off on a capitalised BUT with an ellipsis and is completed after the turn.

notes: on an orange page, three smiling planet and moon faces float together

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
…mostly she likes to do things
for herself.
pages.change: The sentence is completed: mostly she likes to do things for herself
pages.page_turn_note: The statement is complete; the turn returns to the shop.

notes: Livhu raises a spoon high at a counter set with a kettle, a mug, a sugar bowl, a tea box and a milk carton
illustration.only_in_image: What she does for herself is shown, not told: she raises a spoon over a kettle, mug, tea box and milk, making her own tea.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
At the spaza shop she enjoys chatting
to people in the line and making
new friends.
“Hi! I am Livhu.”
pages.change: Back at the shop she waits in line by choice, chats and makes friends
pages.page_turn_note: Callback to the shop spread; the turn returns to the park.

notes: Livhu, holding a bottle, waits in the queue among people with star and moon heads; the cashier leans on the counter
illustration.only_in_image: She holds her own shopping and waits among the queue while the cashier stays behind the counter: the earlier pushing is undone without a word.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Back in the park, she joins in a fun game
of tug-of-war with the other children.
pages.change: Back in the park she joins a tug-of-war with the children
pages.page_turn_note: The game starts at the spread end; the strain comes after the turn.

notes: Livhu grips a rope with a determined face, the two planet-headed children pulling behind her
illustration.only_in_image: Livhu is at the front of the rope with a determined, tongue-out face; the two children from the slope pull behind her.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.change: The rope is pulled to its limit
pages.page_turn_note: The text says only that the rope stretches; the picture shows it tearing. The turn does not answer what happened.

notes: a close-up of the rope against the sky, fraying and pulling apart beside a red ribbon marker
illustration.only_in_image: The rope is fraying and coming apart in the middle: the picture shows it about to snap while the text says only that it stretches.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Livhu is so happy.
Her wheelchair helps her have fun with
her favourite people.
pages.change: Livhu is happy; her wheelchair lets her have fun with her favourite people
pages.page_turn_note: A plain statement; the rope moment is not resolved.

notes: Livhu's sun face, blushing and smiling, alone on a lilac page

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
At night she falls asleep thinking about
more great adventures to have with her
wheelchair and her new besties.
pages.change: At night she falls asleep thinking of more adventures with her new friends
pages.page_turn_note: last page; a wordless vignette follows

notes: Livhu asleep under a starry blanket with soft toys; a crescent moon in the window, fairy lights above
illustration.only_in_image: She sleeps under a constellation blanket with a sun toy and space toys beside her and a crescent moon in the window: the sky motif of the heads becomes her bedroom.

pages.label: OBSERVED
